question: Design review for Torchcall 1.8.0 (WoW Forever guild-recruiting addon, Lua). HARD INVARIANTS that must survive: every who search / whisper / invite / guild-chat line is sent inside a click or keypress handler; NO timers sending anything, NO auto-continue of who searches (council killed an auto-chain on 11-05; do not re-open that door); one press = one action; who answers cap at 50 results; 5s gap between who searches; on the live client the SendWho filter TABLE is blocked, so queries are text like '16-28 c-"Mage"' and live data confirms the class words ARE honored (whoMode=text, no fallback tripped). Current pain, verified in code and the user's live SavedVariables: (P1) when a who answer caps at 50 and the band spans levels lo<hi, onWhoResults splits it into TWO halves queued at the front; sweeping a dense 13-level band costs roughly 2x the presses because every interior node is a wasted capped search. PROPOSAL A: on a capped answer split the band into up to FOUR even slices (per-level when width<=4); a slice that still caps splits again; still one press per search, Continue button shows the queue count. (P2) prospects who ANSWERED pin to the top of the Prospects tab via answered(p) = replied and (status whispered, or status invited and not linked). Rows with status 'invited' show ONLY a Reply button: the Skip button is gated to status new|whispered, so an answered-then-invited prospect who never accepts is pinned FOREVER with no removal path; the user has 13 such stale rows aged 1-2 days. PROPOSAL B: (i) show Skip also on answered rows whose status is invited (ns.Skip already handles any status: sets status=skipped, keeps the contacted record so they are never re-whispered); (ii) answered older than 3 days stops pinning: answered() gains an age window, the row falls to the Contacted tab, data intact, Reply/Answers still work there because they key off inConversation(p) which is independent of answered(); (iii) the header 'Answered N' counts only actionable (fresh, unskipped) answers. PROPOSAL C: when a capped answer reports total==shown==50 the note says 'at least 50 online' instead of 'showing 50 of 50 online' (the server caps the total too). Find real bugs, broken assumptions, bad interactions with the fuzz invariant 'nothing sent outside a press', data-loss risks in B, and anything that quietly re-opens timer-driven sends. Dissent explicitly welcome; do not rubber-stamp. --json --html

If B(i) is implemented as the obvious `if p.status == "new" or p.status == "whispered" or ns.Answered(p)` (`UI.lua:799`), then the exact rows B(ii) ages out (>3 days) have `answered() == false` and **lose the Skip button again**. Also push in reverse order so the lower slice is searched first, matching current behavior. ### F3 — HIGH (Proposal A): "a slice that still caps splits again" must mean *enqueue*, never *send* `onWhoResults` runs from the `WHO_LIST_UPDATE` event, which the fuzz guard treats as outside a press (`inAction == false`, `tests/fuzz.lua:66`). The existing code is safe because it only queues. If the "splits again" step is implemented as an eager loop that calls `ns.NextSearch()` (even gated on the 5s gap via `C_Timer.After`), that is exactly the timer-driven auto-chain the council killed on 11-05 — a who search sent from an event/timer. The 5s gap would also make such a loop self-perpetuating (each answer schedules the next), which is the specific door that must stay shut. Keep A a pure queue-building operation in `onWhoResults`. ### F4 — HIGH (Proposal A): "even slices" assumes a uniform level distribution — a broken assumption, and the signal to fix it is already in hand Even-slice splitting presumes players spread evenly across `[lo,hi]`. They don't — Forever level distributions are heavily skewed toward the cap and low levels. And because of Proposal C's own premise (server caps `total` at 50), the splitter is blind to total density. But it does *not* have to be: `onWhoResults` already reads `info.level` for all 50 returned players (`Core.lua:738-748`) and stores them via `addFromWho`. So B(i), by widening the set of rows that can become `skipped`, grows an already-unbounded accumulation of skipped rows in `db.prospects`, and any future funnel/aged analysis that wants the invite time will find it replaced by the skip time. Not data loss of the thing that matters (`contacted` is preserved — re-whisper is correctly blocked), but a timestamp loss + unbounded growth worth a one-line fix (don't overwrite `p.t` for an already-contacted row). ### F7 — LOW (Proposal B): row and conversation panel disagree about Skip B(i) puts Skip on the invited row, but `refreshTalk()` still hides "They said no" for any status other than `whispered` (`UI.lua:676`). Cosmetic, but confusing. ### F8 — LOW (Proposal C): the trigger must be `total == shown`, not `shown >= 50` "at least 50 online" is only correct when `total == shown == 50`. C is a safe, surgical wording fix; don't let it touch the `total > shown` branch. ### F9 — NOTE (Proposal B(iii)): no new counter is needed — don't add one The header `Answered N` already reads `c.replied` from `Counts()` (`Core.lua:456`, rendered at `UI.lua:684-686`), which is `answered(p)`-based. So "fresh" comes for free from B(ii)'s age window and "unskipped" comes for free from the status clause (skipped/declined rows never satisfy `answered`). The risk is if B(iii) is implemented as a *separate* counter keyed on `p.replied ~= nil` ignoring status/age — that would re-count skipped and aged rows. Just let `c.replied` flow from the updated `answered()`. ### F10 — NOTE: "Continue button shows the queue count" already shipped `UI.lua:721-722` already renders `Continue (%d left)` from `ns.QueueSize()`.
